decision_question: How to design, adapt, and evaluate a from-scratch ~3M parameter Transformer for English grammar correction and paraphrase preference alignment under a 4-week single-GPU budget without generating synthetic labels?

sources.title: TinyStories: How Small Can Language Models Be and Still Speak Coherent English?
sources.limitations: Preprint; demonstrates English syntax acquisition on small parameter budgets (1M-33M) for narrative text, but does not provide instruction-following or grammar editing supervision.

sources.title: CoEdIT: Text Editing by Task-Specific Instruction Tuning
sources.limitations: Preprint; uses T5 foundation models (770M-3B); our 3M model will achieve lower absolute GLEU, making fair baseline comparison and error analysis crucial.

sources.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
sources.limitations: Evaluated primarily on large models (RoBERTa, GPT-2/3); low-rank adaptation on a 3M model requires careful rank selection (r=8) to ensure expressive adapter capacity without overfitting.

sources.title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
sources.limitations: Requires a well-calibrated reference model policy and stable beta coefficient; preference pairs must be strictly paired under identical prompt contexts.

sources.title: JFLEG: A Fluency-Oriented Corpus for GEC Evaluation
sources.limitations: Compact evaluation corpus (747 test sentences) with 4 human reference rewrites; multi-reference GLEU metric must be evaluated without contamination from training sets.

sources.title: deepset/prompt-injections Dataset
sources.limitations: Evaluates known prompt injection vectors; supplemental evaluation only, not an exhaustive jailbreak or safety certification.

claims.statement: KV Cache stores per-layer key and value projection tensors during autoregressive generation, eliminating redundant historical recomputations and ensuring O(1) attention compute per decoded token.
Attaching low-rank adapter matrices to Wq and Wv attention projections with rank r=8 freezes base model weights and reduces trainable parameters by over 80% while preserving editing adaptation.

Direct Preference Optimization trains policy parameters using response-only log-likelihood ratios relative to a frozen reference policy without fitting a separate reward model or executing reinforcement learning rollouts.

Grammar error correction and paraphrase generation are distinct tasks; empirical improvements in paraphrase preference win rate under DPO do not substantiate claims of grammatical error correction capability.
All training and evaluation data must derive exclusively from existing fields in public datasets (tgt, chosen, rejected) without generating synthetic negative pairs or hand-crafted labels.

hypotheses.statement: Self-written LoRA on Wq and Wv will train with >80% fewer trainable parameters and lower peak VRAM than full SFT while retaining at least 85% of full SFT edit competence on validation loss.
hypotheses.falsifiable_test: Execute controlled training runs for C1-full vs C1-lora under identical optimizer and epoch schedules, measuring parameter counts, peak VRAM via torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated(), and held-out validation cross-entropy.

hypotheses.statement: Dynamic KV Cache per-layer will achieve monotonic speedup in next-token latency (TPOT) across context lengths 128, 512, 1024, and 2048 with exact numerical equivalence in generated logits compared to uncached decoding.
hypotheses.falsifiable_test: Run automated profiling benchmark asserting torch.allclose(cached_logits, uncached_logits, atol=1e-5) and recording TTFT, TPOT, and throughput across the 4 context lengths.

hypotheses.statement: DPO alignment on paraphrasing preferences will increase chosen-over-rejected conditional log-likelihood margin on held-out validation pairs relative to the frozen C1-lora baseline policy.
hypotheses.falsifiable_test: Evaluate margin log pi_theta(y_w|x) - log pi_theta(y_l|x) on the 95 validation pairs of alecccdd/paraphrasing-preferences-orpo-dpo before and after DPO training.

decision.chosen_option: Modular PyTorch causal decoder-only LM (~3M params, 4 layers, d_model=256, 4 heads, vocab 2048) with custom KV Cache, self-written LoRA on Wq/Wv, DPO with frozen C1-lora reference, deterministic guardrails, and automated evaluation on JFLEG and held-out preferences.
decision.rationale: Directly satisfies all mandatory examination requirements and Track B specifications while strictly adhering to the 4-week scope, single-GPU hardware budget, and no-labeling data policy.
decision.mitigated_risks: Mitigates capacity limitations by establishing honest baseline evaluations and clear research questions; mitigates memory and latency risks via isolated profiling; mitigates safety vulnerabilities with deterministic application guardrails.

unresolved_uncertainties: Available GPU VRAM during pretraining vs batch size; will run hardware pilot in Week 1
Distribution of sequence lengths in alecccdd/paraphrasing-preferences-orpo-dpo to determine if context_length=128 retains sufficient pairs or requires 256
